title: Gurfateh Pirzada Says Diwali Crackers Burnt His Mumbai Balcony and Room
excerpt: The Lust Stories 3 actor shared photos of a smoke-filled balcony and a damaged room on Instagram Stories, tagged the BMC and Mumbai Police, and shared an AQI screenshot reading 521.
body:
• Actor Gurfateh Pirzada, recently seen in Lust Stories 3, says stray Diwali firecrackers burnt his entire Mumbai balcony and spread into almost his whole room.
  • He posted the aftermath on Instagram Stories — a balcony thick with smoke and a room with belongings moved aside — and tagged the BMC and Mumbai Police.
  • He also shared a screenshot of Mumbai's air quality index reading 521 on Sunday evening and called the city a "gas chamber," questioning governance and accountability.
  • The Bombay High Court has banned bursting firecrackers in public places. On Saturday, the BMC asked 237 corporators to spread awareness about firecracker harm in slums and densely populated areas.

Actor Gurfateh Pirzada has said his Mumbai home was among those hit by firecracker-related fires this Diwali. The Lust Stories 3 actor posted the aftermath on Instagram Stories, saying stray crackers burnt his entire balcony and spread into nearly his whole room, according to Indulge Express and Zoom TV.

What his posts showed

One photo shared by Pirzada shows the balcony thick with smoke. Another shows the room inside, with the curtains drawn back to one side of the bed and some belongings moved around. He tagged the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) and Mumbai Police in the post. Reports of the incident, first carried by India Today and Hindustan Times, describe the damage as caused by firecrackers bursting outside the home on Diwali eve; Pirzada has not detailed how the fire started beyond attributing it to crackers.

"The sheer stupidity of the masses is astounding… crackers burnt my entire balcony and almost my entire room. The entire city is burning and is a gas chamber."

— Gurfateh Pirzada, Instagram Stories, as reported by Hindustan Times

Air quality was the second complaint

Alongside the damage photos, Pirzada shared a screenshot of Mumbai's Air Quality Index (AQI) from Sunday evening, which showed a reading of 521. In a separate Story, he said he was angry at how people behaved the night before, argued that a country keen on having children shows little concern for the air those children breathe, blamed a lack of governance and accountability, and said he was also worried about pets and stray animals during the noise.

His experience came on a night when pollution in Mumbai spiked. Overnight, Navy Nagar recorded an AQI of 497 and several other areas crossed 400, leaving a thick haze over the city in one of its worst air-quality spells of the season. By 7 a.m., Kherwadi had the highest reading among the city's monitoring stations, at 264.

The rules already on paper

The Bombay High Court had banned the bursting of firecrackers in public places. On Saturday, the BMC asked 237 corporators to spread awareness in slums and densely populated areas about the harm firecrackers cause, amid concern over rising air and noise pollution. Pirzada's posts did not say whether he had filed a formal complaint, and neither the BMC nor Mumbai Police has commented on his case in the reports published so far.

Pirzada was recently seen in Lust Stories 3, the latest instalment of the anthology series. His Diwali post adds a celebrity name to a wider Mumbai pattern this festival season: firecracker fires and a sharp post-Diwali pollution spike that civic agencies had warned about in advance.
